column1: # tests/fixtures/filenames.tsv -- what a media server makes of a filename.
# The table is the specification. jfkit.naming reimplements somebody else's
# expressions, so without pinned examples it becomes confidently wrong the day
# those expressions change -- and a parser that is confidently wrong renames
# files into the wrong episodes. Every row here is an invented name.
# Checked against: Jellyfin 12.1 (Emby.Naming at ee91c75e77), September 2026.
# Columns: path, season, episode, end, rule, multi
#   an empty cell means the server produces no number at all
#   rule is the kind of expression that claimed the name (jfkit.naming.Rule):
#     "cross" is an NxNN form, "pair" the unanchored "1-12" expression, which
#     reads the first number as the season, "episode" a number with no season
#   rule "by-date" marks a name whose numbers are re-derived on every refresh
#   "multi" says whether one of the ten multi-episode expressions attached the
#     end number, which happens whatever claimed the name first
# Revised for the full port of the 26 expressions: sixteen rows changed. The
# NxNN rows are claimed by upstream's own expression ("cross", not the old
# "reconstructed"); names the partial port called unclaimed are read by the
# "1-12" pair, "Episode N" and "01 - title" expressions; and the expressions
# are case-insensitive upstream, so an upper-case X in a codec token stops the
# absolute expression exactly as a lower-case one does.
